summaries.demographer: Keith Moore is a 60-year-old White non-Hispanic married man living with his wife Linda in Apache Junction, Arizona (Q84-Q89). He has a high school diploma, is U.S.-born, and spent adolescence in Apache Junction in a two-parent household with one sister (Q90, Q97-Q99). He is retired from paid handyman and repair work and is not in the paid workforce, but he remains active through senior center volunteering (Q16, Q65-Q78). His household is a two-person owner household with a mortgage, modest retirement resources, Linda's part-time income, and careful budgeting (Q51-Q58, Q74).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Keith is highly loss-averse around debt, health costs, and household stability, preferring budgeting, repair, saving, and delayed consumption over credit use (Q57-Q64, Q82-Q83). His choices are motivated by independence, family presence, and practical usefulness, as shown by his earlier decision to choose local handyman work over higher-paying distant construction jobs (Q02-Q03). He responds to uncertainty with routines, lists, emergency savings, and preventive maintenance rather than impulsive spending (Q17, Q61-Q62). He takes moderate physical risks in hiking and ATV activity but adapts after injury, showing bounded risk-taking tied to identity and competence (Q33-Q34, Q44).
summaries.political_scientist: Keith is a regular voter who uses mail ballots and pays close attention to local issues such as water, roads, taxes, public safety, land use, and growth (Q23-Q25). He identifies as an Independent leaning Republican and describes himself as a moderate practical conservative rather than a strong partisan (Q24, Q95-Q96). He has mixed but reform-oriented views on policing and race, supporting accountability and training while rejecting abolishing police (Q26-Q30). His civic orientation is localist and communitarian, expressed through voting, neighbor support, senior center volunteering, and concern for desert stewardship (Q08, Q16, Q23, Q108).
summaries.psychologist: Keith presents as conscientious, pragmatic, self-reliant, and identity-driven around competence, usefulness, and being dependable (Q01, Q65, Q109). He regulates stress through routine, hands-on repair, walking, music, budgeting, and direct conversation with Linda rather than substance use or online support (Q38, Q43-Q50). Retirement and physical limitations challenge his self-concept, but he adapts by teaching, mentoring, pacing his body, and reframing strength as asking for help when needed (Q16, Q33-Q34, Q44). His relational style is loyal, modest, and service-oriented, with family and community mentorship central to his sense of purpose (Q05-Q07, Q108-Q109).
